Methodology / Financial services

How to verify AI recommendations in financial services

Alexey YakovlevUpdated 8 November 2026

Before measuring AI visibility, classify the actual provider, regulated activity and its legal powers. A wrong statement about an insurance or investment provider can matter more than a raw mention.

Discuss your projectSee the industry hub

A good financial recommendation accurately identifies the service and the provider's role, uses current information and avoids promises beyond contractual or legal evidence.

Classify the engagement first

Differentiate accounting outsourcing from independent assurance, and general financial planning from individually tailored investment advice. Check the appropriate registry status when legally applicable.

Separate the insurance broker's role from the insurer's liability, the leasing company's offer from general financing and the payment technology provider from the registered payment operator.

Create an auditable prompt matrix

Split branded prompts from unbranded selection. Record location, buyer type, commercial intent, model, exact prompt text and expected sample size.

BMR counts received answers mentioning the business, divided by all received answers. Report missing runs separately and assess the quality of each recommendation independently.

Verify legal identity, authority and terms

Use Bank of Russia registries where relevant to the provider's activity, not as a blanket test of every firm using finance terminology. A payment interface must not automatically be portrayed as a payment-system operator.

For accounting, verify reporting delegation and electronic signature authority. For insurance, inspect coverage and exclusions; for leasing, identify payment assumptions.

Assess every answer and flag high-impact errors

Keep the raw answer, date, model, named providers and cited evidence.

  • An accountant is described as a statutory auditor: role error.
  • A financial planner is attributed registered investment advice without verification.
  • An insurance broker is described as the claims-paying insurer.
  • A payments interface is assigned a regulated operator status without evidence.
  • A leasing price omits the advance payment, period and purchase terms.

Create a traceable evidence base

Relevant web pages must state the legal identity, service scope, responsibility boundaries, verified registry status and current terms. Publishing the official source near the claim supports a more accurate evaluation.

Do not infer guaranteed returns, insurance payments or error-free accounting from generic marketing language. Distinguish actions taken from measured outcomes.

Repeat baseline measurements

Compare the same prompts and AI interfaces, record unavailable responses and treat new questions as a separate sample. Track factual errors alongside mentions.

Under the GAEO guaranteed plan, BMR targets are +5, +10 and +15 percentage points over the baseline for months 1, 2 and 3 respectively, subject to contract. Commercial revenue impact is a separate measurement.

Frequently asked questions

Can BMR be compared between accountants and payment firms?+
Only with clear disclosure of different samples. Each client should have a tailored prompt matrix and consistent follow-up measurements.
Does a regulator registry entry prove a good customer match?+
No. It establishes the applicable status; service suitability also requires verifiable product and contract information.
What if an AI answer mislabels the regulated provider?+
Log it as a factual accuracy failure even when the company name is counted in BMR.
